mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the following 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during three-month periods of declining RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive momentum in personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) combined with rising housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand, which boosts consumption and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST are above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a macroeconomic slowdown, which depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during two consecutive quarters of declining GDPC1.
